stories.headline: Schools to be closed, response team on alert as Odisha steps up cyclone preparedness
stories.title: Schools to be closed, response team on alert as Odisha steps up cyclone preparedness
stories.summary: The weather system over Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a deep depression on Sunday and into a cyclonic storm by Monday morning and is expected to make landfall on October 28
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With a well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into a deep depression on Sunday (October 25, 2026) before possibly developing into a cyclone, the Odisha government on Saturday (October 24, 2026) stepped up preparedness as part of its efforts to ensure zero casualties with disaster response teams on high alert.

Educational institutions in five Odisha districts will be closed on October 28 and 29 while fishermen along the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coast have been warned not to venture into the sea as per standard advisory.

The well-marked low pressure area over east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal has persisted and is most likely to intensify into a depression on Saturday (October 24), a special bulleting of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.

“Thereafter, it is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression on October 25 and into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by October 26 morning.
Moving west-northwestwards, it would continue to intensify further and reach over west-central Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast around morning of October 28,” the bulletin said.
Experts at the IMD, Amaravati, said the winds could further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm, the first of the year.
Wind speeds are expected to reach 62–88 km per hour in a cyclonic storm and 89–117 km per hour in a severe cyclonic storm.
Reviewing preparedness over the cyclone alert, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said, “we have prior experience in managing floods and cyclones.
Cyclones Dana and Montha were successfully managed.
Along with this, several flood situations have also been successfully handled.

The State government is fully prepared to achieve zero casualty this time too.” Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari and Chief Secretary Anu Garg along with other top officials attended the meeting.
Southern Odisha districts are expected to be impacted with heavy rain under influence of the cyclone as per disaster management authorities.

stories.headline: Odisha braces for cyclone Arnab as storm nears
stories.title: Odisha braces for cyclone Arnab as storm nears
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bhubaneswar: Odisha is bracing for the impact of cyclone Arnab, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting the system to intensify into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal on October 26 and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast by the morning of October 28, leading the state government to step up preparedness measures and set a target of zero casualties.

Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Saturday said the state government had reviewed the possible impact of the cyclone and assigned specific responsibilities to departments to ensure preparedness ahead of the system's expected landfall.
"We have just concluded a review meeting regarding the impact of cyclone Arnab and the measures to tackle it.
According to the Meteorological Department, the cyclone is expected to make landfall on the afternoon of 28 October somewhere between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha.
We have received reports indicating that this will lead to heavy rainfall across various districts in these states...
We have assigned specific responsibilities to each department, ensuring they are fully prepared in advance.
The state government is completely ready to handle this situation.
As always, our primary objective remains the same: Zero casualties," CM Majhi said.
According to the IMD, a well-marked low-pressure area over the central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal intensified as of 8.30 am on Saturday.
The system is likely to persist over the same region and intensify into a depression on October 24, before moving west-northwestwards and strengthening into a deep depression on October 25.

The system is expected to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26 and continue moving west-northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, reaching the region around the morning of October 28.
IMD Bhubaneswar Director Manorama Mohanty said Odisha was likely to be affected by rainfall and wind activity as the system intensified and moved towards the coast.

stories.headline: Odisha activates disaster response as cyclone threatens October 28 landfall
stories.title: Odisha activates disaster response as cyclone threatens October 28 landfall
stories.summary: Odisha activates disaster response as cyclone threatens October 28 landfall
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha has activated disaster response measures as a cyclone is forecast to make landfall on October 28.
Evacuations, closures and emergency deployments aim to protect vulnerable coastal and southern districts.

The Odisha government on Saturday activated its disaster response machinery as a weather system over the Bay of Bengal was expected to develop into a cyclonic storm and make landfall between the northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha coasts on the morning of October 28, news agency PTI reported.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the well-marked low-pressure area was likely to become a depression on Saturday, strengthen into a deep depression on October 25 and develop into a cyclonic storm by the morning of October 26.
"Moving west-northwestwards, it would continue to intensify further and reach west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around the morning of October 28," the IMD said.
IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the system was "likely to make landfall on the morning of October 28 somewhere between northern Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha coasts".

Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed Odisha's preparedness and directed officials to prioritise public safety, evacuation and emergency response, with the aim of preventing casualties, according to PTI.
Majhi said the cyclone could bring heavy rainfall to southern and coastal Odisha, along with gusty winds of 70-90 kmph.
Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts were likely to be the worst affected, while other coastal districts could also receive significant rainfall.
The chief minister directed the authorities to close schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five districts on October 28 and 29.
Collectors in other districts will decide whether to close educational institutions based on the developing situation.
Majhi asked officials to move people from vulnerable areas to safer places.

stories.headline: India colts start on a winning note in Under-15 FIFA World Cup in Baku
stories.title: India colts start on a winning note in Under-15 FIFA World Cup in Baku
stories.summary: India beat Laos 4-2 in their FIFA Under-15 World Cup & Festival opener in Baku, securing the country’s first three points at a FIFA tournament.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
event term: 'world cup' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: Bibiano Fernandes's India began their campaign at the inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup & Festival Azerbaijan 2026 with a 4-2 victory over Laos in their Group K opener at the Hovsan Competition Complex in Baku on Saturday.
Captain Macdonnish Ngairangbam and R Lalremruatfela handed the Blue Colts an early two-goal advantage before Anavin Xayyasone reduced the deficit for Laos.
Souksavanh Siliseng equalised for the Southeast Asians soon after half-time, but India finished strong with Lalremruatfela and Soumojit Sarkar firing from long range to restore the lead.
The win, interestingly enough, secured the nation's first three points at a FIFA tournament.
The tournament features 189 national teams, divided into 32 groups, with matches played in an eight-a-side format.
Each match consists of two 20-minute halves with rolling substitutions permitted.
Fernandes' colts made a bright start on Saturday morning and created two chances in the opening four minutes.
They took the lead in the seventh minute after brilliant footwork from Deepak, who worked his way into the small box before cutting the ball back for Macdonnish to tap home.
The pressure continued to pay off, with India doubling their advantage in the 11th minute.
A Laos clearance was blocked by Deepak, and the ball fell to R Lalremruatfela, who took a touch before slamming home with his left boot.
India will next face Cameroon tomorrow (Sunday, 25th October) in the morning before taking on Grenada later the same day in the evening.
They will conclude the qualification stage against Bahrain and Senegal on Monday - and their results across five matches will determine which performance tier they make the cut for the second phase.

stories.headline: After 30-year wait, Centre sanctions ₹27 cr for Bairakkuppa bridge linking Kerala and Karnataka
stories.title: After 30-year wait, Centre sanctions ₹27 cr for Bairakkuppa bridge linking Kerala and Karnataka
stories.summary: The Centre has sanctioned ₹27 crore for the long-delayed Bairakkuppa Bridge over the Kabani River, reviving a key road link between Wayanad and Karnataka.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ending a nearly three-decade-long wait for a vital cross-border connectivity project, the Centre has sanctioned ₹27 crore for the construction of the Bairakkuppa Bridge across the Kabani River, connecting Wayanad in Kerala with Karnataka.

The bridge, to be built under the Sethubandhan scheme of the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF), will link Perikkalloor village in Wayanad with Bairakkuppa in Karnataka, providing a direct route for thousands of people who currently have to take a circuitous road journey to reach the opposite bank.
Public Works Minister P K Basheer described it as a major breakthrough for the long-pending project.
He said construction would begin soon and credited the efforts of the UDF government in Kerala and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for securing the approval.

Basheer said he had held several rounds of discussions with Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, which eventually led to Karnataka issuing a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the project, removing a key hurdle to its implementation.

The bridge was conceived as a joint initiative by Kerala and Karnataka, with the foundation stone laid on September 24, 1994, by the then chief ministers of the two states, K Karunakaran and Veerappa Moily.
However, the project remained on paper for decades, forcing residents on both sides of the river to rely on longer road routes.
The minister said Public Works Department (PWD) officials would oversee the land acquisition process for the approach roads on both sides of the river.
The Kerala government would bear the cost of acquiring the land, he added.
The need for a permanent connection is underscored by the daily movement of people across the two regions.
Bairakkuppa has a population of around 10,000, while Perikkalloor is home to approximately 28,000 people.
According to Basheer, around 300 to 350 people, including nearly 200 students, travel between the two regions every day.
